title: A future in another city? How migration costs shape young people's college choices: Guest post by Merve Demirel
gist: Job-market paper by Merve Demirel (Stockholm University) using two experiments with 1,682 high-school students in Maharashtra, India: students require more than double the salary to study away from home (women ~3x as much as men), and a peer-mentoring program raised moves only to nearby in-district colleges, not distant hubs like Pune and Mumbai. Implies migration frictions are emotional/safety-driven and need destination-side fixes, not just information.

insights.claim: Indian high-school students in Maharashtra are indifferent between a college at home and one away only if migrating more than doubles their expected salary.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Non-monetary migration frictions are huge, slowing spatial convergence of labor and human capital in emerging markets.
insights.quote: students are indifferent between colleges at home and away only if migrating more than doubles their expected salary
insights.locator: On average, students are indifferent between

insights.claim: Women in the Maharashtra study require about three times as much salary gain as men to be willing to migrate for college.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Gendered mobility frictions cap female labor supply to high-productivity urban centers in India.
insights.quote: with women requiring about three times as much as men
insights.locator: On average, students are indifferent between

insights.claim: Perceived migration costs rise sharply with distance: a move to a nearby city within the district is seen as very different from a move to major education hubs several hours away.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Secondary cities may capture migration flows more cheaply than megacity hubs.
insights.locator: The required increase rises with distance

insights.claim: Observed monetary costs such as transport are usually too small to explain why people do not migrate despite large spatial income gaps, pointing to unobserved psychological and social costs.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Policies targeting only cash/transport costs will under-deliver on mobility.
insights.locator: A central puzzle in economics is

insights.claim: More than half of students expect studying away to yield higher salaries even after living costs, yet most still prefer to study near home.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Returns are understood; frictions, not information on returns, are binding.

insights.claim: Going beyond one's home district can expand the number of college programs a student typically qualifies for roughly tenfold, with the most selective programs concentrated in Pune and Mumbai.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Educational opportunity is highly concentrated geographically in India.
insights.quote: can expand the number of programs they could typically qualify for by tenfold
insights.locator: Students in my study come from

insights.claim: Students expect to feel less safe, less happy, lonelier, with weaker family ties, lower parental approval and more difficulty managing daily life when away from home; women are especially concerned about safety, parental approval and what others think.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Safety and social norms are the binding constraints on female mobility.

insights.claim: Nearly 30 percent of students know no one to ask for college advice, and half have no relatives or friends in other destinations.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Thin information networks persist in rural/peri-urban India.
insights.quote: Nearly 30 percent know no one to ask for college advice

insights.claim: Randomly offering phone-based peer mentorship with a college student who had migrated raised applications to study away from home by four percentage points (from 34%) and actual moves by three points (from 22%).
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Light-touch, cheap interventions shift behavior modestly.
insights.locator: Students offered mentorship became more likely

insights.claim: Mentorship-induced applications and moves stayed within the home district; there was no increase toward the distant hubs where mentors themselves study.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Peer contact does not overcome big-distance frictions; megacity talent pipelines won't be fixed by information alone.
insights.quote: There was no corresponding increase toward the more distant hubs, where the mentors study.

insights.claim: Mentorship effects were driven entirely by men, whose applications away from home rose by ten percentage points, while women's did not change and their expectations of distant cities became, if anything, less favorable.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Information can even worsen women's perceptions; gender gaps in mobility may widen under info-only policies.
insights.locator: The effects were driven by men

insights.claim: Light-touch interventions such as information on living costs or scholarships may work for short moves where migration costs are small, but not for long moves to large cities where gains are largest.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Expect diminishing returns from info programs for megacity migration.

insights.claim: Expanding colleges in smaller towns brings education closer but risks leaving graduates in places with fewer good jobs if good jobs require later migration.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Decentralized education investment has a hidden cost if jobs remain agglomerated.
insights.locator: A natural response to large migration

insights.claim: Connecting students to distant opportunity may require lowering destination-side costs such as safe housing, moving help, and ongoing post-arrival support.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Opportunity for student housing/support services in Indian education hubs.
insights.quote: lowering migration costs at the destination, such as providing safe housing, practical help with moving, or support that continues after arrival
insights.locator: A natural response to large migration
